chunks.arabic_text: الكَافِي: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى، عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ، عَنْ جَمِيلَ بْنِ صَالِحٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: إِنَّ الَّذِي يَعْلَمُ الْعِلْمَ مِنْكُمْ لَهُ أَجْرٌ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ الْمُتَعَلِّمِ وَلَهُ الْفَضْلُ عَلَيْهِ، فَتَعَلَّمُوا الْعِلْمَ مِنْ حَمَلَةِ الْعِلْمِ وَعَلِّمُوهُ إِخْوَانَكُمْ كَمَا عَلَّمُوكُمُ الْعُلَمَاءُ

translations.en: Indeed, the one who teaches the knowledge among you has a reward equal to the reward of the student, and he has superiority over him; so seek knowledge from the bearers of knowledge and teach it to your brothers as the scholars taught it to you.

en.summary: This hadith highlights the virtue of teaching knowledge, stating that the teacher receives a reward equal to that of the student, with additional merit for the teacher. It instructs believers to acquire knowledge from its bearers and to pass it on to their brethren just as they were taught by the scholars.
en.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for teaching knowledge compared to learning it?
